description: Concurred, argued that the impeachment petition was invalid, did not allege impeachable offenses, and the hearing denied due process, violating the separation of powers doctrine.

name: Justice Thompson
description: Concurred, argued that impeachment should be reserved for serious criminal conduct and not for political disagreements or unpopular decisions, emphasizing the Supreme Court's role in interpreting the Constitution.

name: Justice Nickell
description: Dissented, argued that the court's supervisory writ overstepped judicial authority by intruding on the legislature's exclusive impeachment power, which is not subject to judicial review, and that the legislature retains discretion to define impeachable offenses.

name: Justice Goodwine
description: Not sitting on the case due to a pending impeachment inquiry against her.

name: BISIG, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that sovereign immunity bars claims for monetary relief for funds due to the state, even if unlawfully collected, but does not bar claims for a refund of funds never due to the state or constitutional takings claims.

name: Lambert, C.J.

name: Justice Keller
description: Concurred, argued that HB 9 is unconstitutional because charter schools are not 'common schools' as defined by the Kentucky Constitution and statutory law, and funding them with public money without voter approval creates an unmonitored, non-uniform parallel system.

name: Lambert, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that HB 9 violates the Constitution by permitting common school funds to support charter schools without voter approval, and that the General Assembly ceded its constitutional authority to oversee public schools to authorizers, making charter schools non-unitary.

name: Thompson, J.
description: Concurred with Chief Justice Lambert's separate opinion.

name: JUSTICE, THOMPSON
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court erred in allowing a key witness to testify remotely for convenience, violating the defendant's confrontation rights, which was not harmless beyond a reasonable doubt for the trafficking convictions, but was harmless for other convictions.

name: Justice Bisig
description: Concurred, argued that SB 1 violates Section 59 of the Kentucky Constitution because it treats the Jefferson County public school district differently from others without a reasonable or natural basis, thus constituting special or local legislation.

name: Justice Keller

name: Justice Nickell
description: Dissented, argued that the rehearing was improvidently granted, as the original majority opinion correctly applied the Woodall test and the new majority effectively overruled Woodall based on a change in court composition, not legal error.

name: Chief Justice Lambert
description: Dissented, joined Justice Nickell's opinion that the rehearing was improvidently granted and the original majority's decision should stand.

name: Justice Conley

name: VANMETER CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the legislature has condoned the Parole Board's power to issue serve-outs for life sentences, which does not violate separation of powers as parole is an executive function and serve-outs do not alter judicially-imposed sentences.

name: KELLER, J.
description: Concurred in result only, argued that the Board's serve-out decisions for life sentences are equivalent to life without parole, raising concerns about the lack of guidance, inadequate time for review, and insufficient external checks on the unelected Board's significant and potentially arbitrary power, which impacts fundamental liberty rights and public health.

name: Thompson, J.
description: Concurred, joining Keller, J.'s opinion regarding concerns about the Parole Board's unfettered discretion and its impact on inmates' liberty.

name: Justice Bisig
description: Concurred, argued that the legislative apportionment plans are constitutional as they do not involve unconstitutional partisan gerrymandering, violate free and equal elections, equal protection, free speech, assembly, or Section 33's dual mandate of population equality and county integrity.

name: Chief Justice VanMeter
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: Justice Nickell
description: Concurred with the majority's decision on the merits of claims under Sections 6 and 33 of the Kentucky Constitution, but dissented, arguing that other claims should have been dismissed as non-justiciable political questions due to a lack of clear judicial standards for partisan gerrymandering.

name: Justice Thompson
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: Justice Keller
description: Concurred with most of the majority opinion but dissented from the holding regarding Section 33, arguing that HB 2 violates Section 33 by unnecessarily splitting and combining counties more times than necessary, thereby diluting its explicit requirements for county integrity.

name: Justice Conley
description: Dissented, arguing that the Appellants lacked standing to bring their claims, as their alleged injuries were not concrete, particularized, and actual to individual voters, but rather to institutional and collective interests of the democratic party.

name: KELLER, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court did not commit reversible errors in the case, and therefore, the convictions should be affirmed.

name: LAMBERT, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that abortion providers have first-party standing to challenge the trigger ban but lack standing to challenge the heartbeat ban or to assert third-party claims for patients, and affirmed the dissolution of the temporary injunction.

name: THOMPSON, J.

name: NICKELL, J.

name: MINTON CHIEF JUSTICE

name: CONLEY, JUSTICE
